claims.location: source name SILAC light rows 222 rows, 1-6 ... 433-438
claims.evidence: Label key sheet "SILAC" lists 37 Sample IDs, each with its raw file pattern (e.g. AML1001_Blasts_BM -> AML1001_Blast_BM_2D_Fxx.raw). All 37 keyed groups are annotated. The 38th deposited group, AML1036_Blast_BLD_2D_F01-F06, is absent from that sheet and from the deposited MaxQuant search (which holds an AML1089 group instead; by RunHeader scan count these six deposited raws are exactly the files searched as AML1089_Blast_BLD_2D_F01-F06, review round 2); its identity would rest on the file name only, so its 6 raws are left out (review round 1, IMPORTANT 1; annotations/BLOCKED.md). Suffix _SILAC distinguishes these sample preparations from the same patients' TMT samples.

claims.value: SILAC light = patient blasts; SILAC heavy = spike-in standard
claims.evidence: MaxQuant summary_new.txt: Multiplicity 2, Labels0 empty, Labels1 Arg10;Lys8 on all 228 searched runs (rule 14 verified: really multiplexed SILAC). The patient material is cryopreserved primary cells sorted by FACS and lysed directly (PRIDE sampleProcessingProtocol; Supplemental Methods "Nucleic acid and protein extraction") - no culture step, so it cannot carry a metabolic label: patient = light. Data check (proteinGroups_new.txt): HBB (haemoglobin from blood/marrow specimens) Intensity L >> H in all 38 experiments (e.g. AML1024 L 5.9e10 vs H 1.5e8), and MPO L > H in most - the light channel holds the clinical specimen, the heavy channel cultured (labelled) cells; total L and H intensities are ~1:1 (H/L 0.57-1.14), consistent with a 1:1 spike-in.

claims.location: source name / characteristics[sample type] / characteristics[phenotype] SILAC heavy rows 222 rows, 7-12 ... 439-444
claims.value: SILAC heavy reference standard (spiked into <Sample ID>) / reference / "SILAC heavy (Arg10/Lys8) labelled spike-in reference standard, composition not reported"
claims.evidence: Rule 18: the heavy channel of a spiked-in labelled standard is encoded as reference, not as a study sample. Its composition (which cell line(s)) is not stated in the paper, PRIDE, the label key or the search output, so organism part, cell type, pooled sample, disease, material type, age, sex and individual are not available and no cell line is named. One heavy source per patient mix (37 sources) is an encoding ASSUMPTION, not a sourced fact: nothing states whether one standard batch was spiked into every mix (see limitations). Same encoding as campaign precedent PXD030422.

PRIDE organisms NEWT:9606. Heavy rows: the search used a human-only FASTA (uniprot_taxonomy_9606_Reviewed.fasta) and heavy intensities pair 1:1 with light across thousands of human protein groups, so the standard is human material.

claims.value: bone marrow / blood (from label key Source BM / PB / Apheresis); not available for AML1027
claims.evidence: SILAC sheet column "Source": BM -> bone marrow; PB and Apheresis (leukapheresis product = peripheral blood) -> blood. AML1027 (rows 433-438): Sample ID AML1027_Blasts_BLD and file name "BLD" contradict Source "BM" (also BM in the FH UW45 sheet) -> not available.
The samples are FACS-sorted viable leukemic blasts (uVLBs) (PRIDE protocol; paper). CL:0001064 malignant cell; same choice as campaign precedent PXD030422.

claims.location: characteristics[phenotype] + characteristics[genotype] + factor value[genotype] SILAC light rows
claims.value: blast immunophenotype from label key "Blast IP"; "FLT3-ITD <Pos/Neg/ND>; NPM1 mutation <Pos/Neg>" from label key
claims.evidence: SILAC sheet columns Blast IP (VLBCD34+ / VLBCD117+ / VLBCD45/SSC; legend in Table S13 and Fig. 2: CD117+ = CD34-negative, CD45/SSC = double negative) and FLT3-ITD / NPM1. Genotype is the compared variable: the study compares FLT3-ITD and NPM1 mutant vs non-mutant blasts (paper Results; Table S15).
All patients are de novo AML (PRIDE protocol; paper). MONDO:0018874 verified in OLS. Heavy rows: not available (standard of unreported origin).

claims.location: characteristics[biological replicate] SILAC light rows / SILAC heavy rows
claims.value: 1..n per factor value[genotype] group (groups of 19, 8, 5, 4 and 1 patients) / 1
claims.evidence: Spec sdrf-proteomics/README.adoc:327-341 ('Numbering restarts per experimental condition (factor value group)'; patient_001 = 1, patient_002 = 2) and campaign rule 3; curated precedent PXD003822-freshfrozen-silac numbers its patients 1..4. Numbers are assigned 1..n within each factor-value group in sorted order of characteristics[individual] (unidentified channels, individual not available, keyed by source name); every row of the same individual in a group shares the number (full map: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/a98b4c07-45f2-5d08-aa74-0c95b1e5e538/scratchpad/fix-PXD029216/biological_replicate_map.tsv, written by apply_fixes_r3.py; review round 3 IMPORTANT). Each SILAC patient is one independent sample (one sorted blast lysate, one group). Heavy rows (reference, factor value not applicable) keep 1: they are assumed to be the same standard material in every mix; numbering per mix would assert 37 independent standards, and 'pooled' would assert an unreported pooled composition.

claims.location: characteristics[treatment status] / characteristics[treatment response] / characteristics[clinical data] / characteristics[age] / characteristics[sex] (SILAC rows); characteristics[developmental stage] (SILAC rows except below)
claims.evidence: None of the 37 SILAC patients is in Table S13 and no other individual-level clinical source was deposited (rule 18).

Individual-level source: the label key NPM1 sheet gives Age_Group = Adult for AML1003, AML1006, AML1009, AML1014, AML1018, AML1022, AML1031, AML1034, AML1037, AML1038 (their NPM1-arm samples). Age group is a property of the individual, so the same value is used on these individuals' SILAC light rows (60 rows), matching the TMT file (review round 1, minor 3). EFO:0001272 adult. All other SILAC individuals have no individual-level age or age group -> not available; heavy rows (reference of unknown composition) -> not available.
Raw headers of AML1001, AML1036 (since removed) and AML1027_R2 F01: "Orbitrap Fusion Method Summary"; acquired 4/5/2016 and 6/15/2016. PRIDE instruments also Orbitrap Fusion.

claims.value: beam-type collision-induced dissociation / 27% NCE / linear ion trap
claims.evidence: Method 012616_Trap_Univ_..._ddMS2_IT_HCD_27CE: ActivationType = HCD, Collision Energy (%) = 27, MS2 Detector Type = IonTrap. MS:1000422, MS:1000291 verified.

claims.location: comment[proteomics data acquisition method] all rows
claims.evidence: Method name ddMS2 (data-dependent MS2, top speed 3 s).

No digestion protocol is published for the SILAC arm. MaxQuant summary_new.txt Enzyme = Trypsin, Enzyme mode = Specific; PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol "tryptic enzyme constraint". A specific-trypsin search identifying >6000 protein groups is consistent with a tryptic digest; the column permits only not applicable as a reserved word.
Each patient mix was acquired as 6 runs _2D_F01.._F06; MaxQuant summary Fraction 1-6 per experiment.
MaxQuant 1.5.3.30 parameters.txt "MS/MS tol. (ITMS) 0.5 Da" (MS2 in the ion trap per raw headers).

The SILAC search is AML_SWOG_1st, MaxQuant 1.5.3.30 (parameters.txt); parameters.txt records no precursor/peptide tolerance, summary_new.txt neither, and the zip holds no mqpar.xml. The only stated value, "Peptide MH+ mass tolerances were set at 20 ppm" (PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol, Supplemental Methods), describes the discovery-cohort searches with MaxQuant 1.6.0.1 / 1.6.10.43 (= the TMT searches AML_SWOG_2nd / AML_NPM1); the SILAC arm is not described anywhere. Review round 2 (IMPORTANT): 20 ppm unsupported for this search -> not available (allowed by TERMS.tsv / ms-proteomics 1.2.0). The searches did run, so not applicable would be wrong.

claims.location: comment[data file] / comment[fraction identifier] rows of AML1005, AML1016, AML1029, AML1038 (deposited names kept)
claims.value: deposited file names and F01-F06 -> fraction 1-6, despite different acquisition names in the raw headers
claims.evidence: All 228 SILAC raw headers scanned (silac_acq_check.py -> silac_acq_discrepancies.tsv): only 4 groups disagree with their deposited names. AML1005: F01-F05 carry RO50063 F02-F06 names, F06 carries JK033016_Yeast_p1D_QC_041916_01. AML1016: F01-F05 carry RO50260 F02-F06 names, F06 carries JK033016_Blank_050316_01. AML1029: F06 carries JK033016_AML_RO50145_2D_F06_160523090903 (RO50145 is the specimen code of every AML1012 run). AML1038: F01-F05 carry RO10009 F02-F06 names, F06 carries RO10009 F06b. Resolution by data (reviewer-supplied evidence, reproduced): per-run log2 H/L protein profiles from evidence_new.txt correlated against each experiment's F01-F05 consensus rank the deposited patient first for every F06: AML1005_Blast_BLD_2D_F06 r = 0.8555 to its own patient's F01-F05 consensus (999 proteins, rank 1/38; next best AML1038 r = 0.8171; AML1012 r = 0.4264); AML1016_Blast_BLD_2D_F06 r = 0.8934 to its own patient's F01-F05 consensus (675 proteins, rank 1/38; next best AML1034 r = 0.8375; AML1012 r = 0.5949); AML1029_Blast_BLD_2D_F06 r = 0.8385 to its own patient's F01-F05 consensus (1137 proteins, rank 1/38; next best AML1027 r = 0.7476; AML1012 r = 0.6884); AML1038_Blast_BLD_2D_F06 r = 0.8871 to its own patient's F01-F05 consensus (734 proteins, rank 1/38; next best AML1005 r = 0.8868; AML1012 r = 0.5414). The reviewer reports the same ranking (r = 0.852, 0.886, 0.825, 0.886). MaxQuant searched all four groups under the deposited names. The deposited names and fractions are therefore kept; see limitations for the residual uncertainty.

limitations: techsdrf is not installed; instrument, activation, collision energy and MS2 detector were read from HTTP-range raw headers of one file per run group (9 files), not from every file. Review round 1 added a scan of the first 200 kB of all 228 SILAC and 408 TMT headers (reviewer-fetched; scan_headers.py) for acquisition names and FAIMS settings.

Precursor mass tolerance is not recorded in any deposited MaxQuant parameters.txt/summary.txt. For the SILAC search (AML_SWOG_1st, MaxQuant 1.5.3.30) no source states it, so this file has precursor mass tolerance not available on the 432 searched rows (review round 2). For the TMT MaxQuant searches, 20 ppm is the value the PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol and Supplemental Methods state ("Peptide MH+ mass tolerances were set at 20 ppm"). MaxQuant's main-search default is 4.5 ppm (first search 20 ppm), so the stated value may describe the first search.
Ancestry is not reported for any individual: characteristics[ancestry category] = not available on all rows.

Individual-level age, sex, treatment response and clinical data exist only for the 30 Table S13 patients (SWOG27 + FHCC/UW-HDR3). They were propagated by patient ID to the same patients' samples in other arms (AML1050, AML039, AML044, AML058, AML158, AML179, AML185 in the NPM1 arm); all other patients carry not available. Sex/channel concordance was checked with RPS4Y1 reporter intensity: 27/27 SWOG27 channels and 7/7 NPM1-arm overlap channels agree with Table S13 (AML179: Table S13 sex F but karyotype 46,XY[20]; RPS4Y1 is low in both of its channels, so sex female was kept).

No patient age, sex or individual-level clinical data were deposited for the SILAC-arm, NPM1-arm or E3 patients other than the S13 overlaps; the NPM1 label key gives only Age_Group (Adult/Ped), used for developmental stage (adult) and clinical data (pediatric).

SCOPE NOTE: this file covers 222 of the 228 deposited SILAC runs (37 patients; 444 rows = 222 runs x 2 channels). Left out (annotations/BLOCKED.md, review round 1 IMPORTANT 1): AML1036_Blast_BLD_2D_F01.raw ... F06.raw - the SILAC sheet of the label key has no AML1036 row, the deposited MaxQuant search (summary_new.txt) has no AML1036 experiment but an AML1089_Blast_BLD_2D_F01-F06 experiment whose MS+MS/MS counts equal the RunHeader scan counts of these six raws exactly (review round 2: the same files, searched under another patient's name; AML1036 is NPM1-mutant, AML1089 NPM1 wild-type), and the raw headers carry acquisition name JK033016_AML_RO10001_2D_Fxx, so the patient identity rests on the file name alone. Overall 630 of 636 deposited raws are annotated. The 408 TMT runs are in PXD029216-tmt.sdrf.tsv (rule 12).

The composition of the heavy (Arg10/Lys8) SILAC standard is not reported anywhere (paper, supplement, PRIDE, label key, MaxQuant output); heavy rows are encoded as a reference of unknown composition. The SILAC arm itself is not described in the publication.

AML1027_Blast_BLD_2D_R2_F01-F06 (12 rows) is not covered by the deposited MaxQuant search (which instead names undeposited AML1027 (non-R2) runs, and AML1089 runs that are the deposited AML1036_* raws). Its tolerances are not applicable (rule 5); its modification parameters repeat the arm's SILAC chemistry. Its identity is documented by the label key (SILAC sheet raw pattern AML1027_Blast_BLD_2D_R2_Fxx). Because convert-openms cannot parse "not applicable" tolerances, `parse_sdrf convert-openms` fails on the full SILAC file and succeeds on the searched rows; see validation.txt.
Raw headers show original acquisition names (e.g. RO50479 for AML1027_R2, RO10001 for the left-out AML1036 group): the deposited files were renamed; the name->patient mapping is the submitter's.
AML1027 organism part: Sample ID/file name say BLD, label-key Source says BM -> not available.

Raw-header acquisition names disagree with the deposited names for AML1005 (F01-F05 named F02-F06 of RO50063; F06 named as a yeast QC run), AML1016 (F01-F05 named F02-F06; F06 named as a blank), AML1029 (F06 named RO50145 = AML1012's specimen code) and AML1038 (F01-F05 named F02-F06; F06 named F06b). The per-run L/H profile check (reviewer-supplied, reproduced in silac_f06_profile.tsv) ranks the deposited patient first for every F06, so identity and fraction numbers follow the deposited names. Residual uncertainty: AML1038 F06 is only marginally closer to AML1038 than to AML1005 (r 0.8871 vs 0.8868), and the off-by-one fraction names of AML1005/1016/1038 F01-F05 cannot be checked with profiles (fractions of one mix share the patient's L/H profile), so comment[fraction identifier] for these 3 groups is the deposited numbering.

Developmental stage: adult for the 10 SILAC individuals with an individual-level Age_Group (Adult) in the label key NPM1 sheet; not available for the other 27 SILAC individuals (no individual-level age source).

AML1019_Blast_BM_2D_F06.raw (rows of AML1019 F06, light + heavy) contributed no spectra to the deposited search: AML_SWOG_1st summary_new.txt lists it with MS = 0 and MS/MS = 0, and the reviewer's read of the deposited file's Thermo RunHeader reports only 293 scans (file apparently truncated/not finalised; review round 2). It is kept: it is a deposited raw of a documented group and was submitted to the search (fragment tolerance 0.5 Da kept), but it carries no usable data.

Heavy reference encoding is an assumption: the heavy (Arg10/Lys8) standard is encoded as one reference source per patient mix (37 sources, 'SILAC heavy reference standard (spiked into <Sample ID>)'). No source says whether a single standard batch was prepared once and spiked into every mix; if it was, these 37 sources are one biological sample. The (file, label) pair is unique either way, so this choice is not needed for row uniqueness.

Biological replicate numbering (review round 3): light rows 1..n per factor value[genotype] group in patient-ID order (the order carries no meaning). Heavy reference rows keep 1 under the single-standard-material assumption stated above; if each mix had its own independently prepared standard, they would need 1..37.
